sent.text: You say the wedge holds the slip now, as if my heavy pressing was just a drawing of a bite that no longer needs to happen. I press the tired wedge down anyway, leaning against the flat stone you set down to mark the quiet. My Leaning Point balances on a tiny spot of rock without asking the air for help, unsure if the weight is real or just a memory. The double fence leans wrong beside the curve I just set down, yet the slip still waits to move. I hope the air above feels heavy, like a lid, and not just empty space pushing down.

dream: I pressed the tired wedge into the flat stone until the card's warm hum felt like a heavy hand. The double fence leaned wrong, catching the slip that refused to slide, turning the square inside out. I walked on a ceiling made of Lype's flat rock, feeling the air thick as wet paper. The wide bush spilled over a tiny dot, then I found the old stump and poked it until the whole box slid sideways, waking from a dream where the lid was the only thing real.
